summary: Woodcrest sits in unincorporated Riverside County between the city of Riverside to the north and Perris to the south, spread across 11.4 square miles of gently rolling inland terrain — and what jumps out first is that median household income here runs nearly $140,000, making it one of the higher-earning census-designated places in the Inland Empire, a region more commonly associated with affordability than affluence. That income buys a median home around $679,400, yielding a home-price-to-income ratio under 5:1 — genuinely manageable by Southern California standards, though median rent at $2,875 still consumes a meaningful share of a median paycheck. The tradeoff is geographic: Woodcrest functions as a bedroom community, with most employment concentrated in Riverside, March Air Reserve Base's logistics corridor, or the healthcare systems anchored downtown, meaning commutes along the 215 or Van Buren Boulevard are part of the daily rhythm. The landscape is open and sun-drenched — averaging 10 hours of sunshine a day with highs around 78°F — with views stretching toward the Box Springs Mountains and the distant San Bernardinos. Evening walks happen along quiet residential roads rather than any walkable commercial strip; retail and dining require a short drive. Woodcrest delivers Inland Empire space and income headroom, but asks you to accept that almost everything beyond your front door starts with a car key.
